content.value_statement: Trading backtests often overstate performance because they ignore bias, costs, and uncertainty. This skill provides practical structures for realistic simulation and validation.
actual_capabilities: Designs event-driven simulations with orders, fills, positions, slippage, and commissions.
Provides a vectorized backtesting pattern for simple signal-based strategies.
Structures rolling or anchored walk-forward optimization with separate test periods.
Applies bootstrap Monte Carlo analysis to drawdowns, loss probability, and return intervals.
Calculates return, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, drawdown, win rate, and profit factor metrics.
limitations: It does not execute live trades or connect to brokers.
It does not acquire, clean, or verify historical market data.
The examples require adaptation and testing for each strategy and market.
Backtest results do not guarantee future performance and are not investment advice.

prompt_templates.title: Define a Basic Backtest
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a backtest for [strategy] using [market] data from [period]. Include assumptions, signal timing, transaction costs, and evaluation metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first strategy test

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Simulation Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare event-driven and vectorized designs for [strategy]. Recommend one based on order complexity, data volume, execution realism, and maintenance needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Walk-Forward Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a walk-forward validation plan for [strategy]. Specify training, validation, and test windows. Explain parameter selection and leakage controls.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Advanced Methodology
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this backtesting methodology: [details]. Assess bias, cost modeling, capacity, overfitting, regime sensitivity, Monte Carlo uncertainty, and reporting gaps. Prioritize corrections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Senior reviewer challenging a production research process

output_examples.input: Design a daily momentum backtest with realistic assumptions.
output: Use point-in-time daily bars and generate each signal after the close.
Execute on the next bar and model commission, slippage, and position limits.
Reserve the final period for testing and report drawdown with risk-adjusted returns.

output_examples.input: How should I validate three strategy parameters?
output_examples.output: Use rolling walk-forward windows. Select parameters only on each training window, evaluate the next unseen period, and combine only out-of-sample results.

output_examples.input: Which uncertainty checks should accompany the Sharpe ratio?
output_examples.output: Report maximum drawdown, downside risk, trade count, and parameter stability. Bootstrap returns to estimate loss probability and plausible drawdown ranges.

best_practices: Use point-in-time data and delay signal execution to prevent look-ahead bias.
Model commissions, slippage, market impact, liquidity, and portfolio constraints.
Keep an untouched test period and report uncertainty alongside average performance.
anti_patterns: Optimizing parameters across the full history and reporting the same period.
Testing only surviving securities or using revised data unavailable at the decision time.
Presenting gross returns without costs, capacity limits, drawdowns, or uncertainty.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It supports historical simulation design and does not provide broker connectivity or live execution.

faq.question: Can it obtain market data?
faq.answer: No. You must provide suitable historical data and verify its quality, timestamps, adjustments, and point-in-time accuracy.

faq.question: When should I use an event-driven backtester?
faq.answer: Use it when order lifecycle, multiple assets, execution timing, partial fills, or portfolio state require detailed simulation.

faq.question: When is a vectorized design appropriate?
faq.answer: Use it for simple signal strategies where speed matters and execution behavior can be represented accurately with array operations.

faq.question: Does walk-forward testing eliminate overfitting?
faq.answer: No. It reduces leakage and measures stability, but repeated experimentation can still overfit the research process.

faq.question: Are the performance estimates financial advice?
faq.answer: No. Historical estimates are uncertain, depend on modeling assumptions, and do not guarantee future results.
